questions.q: State what is meant by a character set.

markPoints.concept: the set of characters a computer can use, each with its own binary code
markPoints.exemplar: The characters a computer can represent, each with its own binary code.

questions.example: The collection of characters a computer can use, with a unique binary code for each one.
questions.paraphrase: A list of every symbol the machine knows, each given its own number in binary.
questions.feedback: A set of characters AND the codes for them. Either half on its own is not the definition.

questions.q: ASCII uses 7 bits for each character. How many different characters can it represent?
questions.feedback: 2⁷ = 128. Extended ASCII adds an eighth bit and gets 256.

questions.q: Explain why Unicode was developed when ASCII already existed.

markPoints.concept: ASCII does not have enough codes for the characters of every language
accept: not enough|too few|only 128|only 256|limited|cannot represent|ran out|no room
markPoints.exemplar: ASCII does not have enough codes for every language's characters.

markPoints.concept: Unicode uses more bits, so it can represent far more characters
accept: more bits|16 bits|32 bits|more codes|more characters|far more|thousands|millions
markPoints.exemplar: Unicode uses more bits per character, so it can represent far more of them.

questions.example: ASCII has only 128 codes, which is nowhere near enough for the characters used by every language in the world. Unicode uses more bits for each character, so it can represent many thousands of them, including emoji.
questions.paraphrase: There were far too few codes in ASCII for all the world's alphabets, so a system with more bits per symbol was needed.
questions.feedback: Not enough codes, then what Unicode does about it.

questions.q: In ASCII, the code for 'A' is 65. What is the code for 'C'?
questions.feedback: The letters run in order, so C is two after A. 97 is lower-case 'a'.

questions.q: A plain text file uses 8 bits per character and contains 500 characters. Calculate its size in bytes.
questions.feedback: 8 bits is one byte, so 500 characters is 500 bytes.

questions.q: A text file holds 500 characters in a character set that uses 8 bits per character. What is its file size in bits?
questions.feedback: One character, one code, 8 bits each. The file size is just the number of characters multiplied by that.

questions.q: How does a computer store the letter K?
options: As a binary number given to it by a character set
As a tiny picture of the letter
As the shape of the letter in the font
As the word 'K' in the operating system
questions.feedback: Every character has a number, and the number is stored in binary like everything else. The font decides how it is drawn, not how it is stored.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.2 Lesson 12 — Character foundry, station 1: Text as numbers

questions.q: Explain why two computers need to use the same character set to exchange text correctly.

markPoints.concept: a character set decides which number stands for which character
markPoints.exemplar: A character set decides which number stands for which character.

markPoints.concept: so with different sets the same number would be shown as a different character
markPoints.exemplar: So the same number would be shown as a different character on the other computer.

questions.example: A character set is an agreement about which number means which character. If the sending computer uses one agreement and the receiving one uses another, the same binary number is read as a different character, and the text arrives as nonsense.
questions.paraphrase: The set is what links each code to a particular symbol, so if the two machines use different ones the identical number is displayed as the wrong character.
questions.feedback: What a character set decides, and what goes wrong when the two disagree.
